paper_title: Low-Energy Supernovae Severely Constrain Radiative Particle Decays
notes: Headline result: red-shaded excluded region in Fig. 3 (MainPlot.pdf), the reference case with energy deposition E_mantle < 0.1 B and progenitor radius R* = 5e13 cm (Garching SN model). Contour extracted from the vector fill paths of the e-print figure MainPlot.pdf; axes calibrated against tick marks (x: m_a in MeV, y: G_agamma in GeV^-1, both log). The exclusion is a CLOSED region: points trace the boundary as a loop - down the left edge at m=1 MeV (plot clip), along the lower boundary (G ~ 4.4e-9 GeV^-1 x (MeV/m_a) below ~10 MeV, minimum ~2.0e-10 GeV^-1 near 120-150 MeV), around the rightmost extent at ~480 MeV, then back along the upper (trapping-regime) boundary, which is clipped at the plot top (G ~ 4e-7 GeV^-1) for m_a < ~110 MeV; the closing run along the plot-top clip returns to m=1 MeV. Hence masses are not monotonic. G_agamma uses the standard convention (decay rate Gamma = G^2 m^3/64pi), identical to canonical g_agamma. Astrophysical energy-deposition bound: no formal confidence level stated and no dark-matter density assumed. The alternative curves (R*=3e12 cm dotted, 1 B thin, one-zone blue) were not used.
